facts.statement: Oplosaurus is known from a single tooth that has often been linked to the genus Pelorosaurus, but there is no solid evidence supporting this connection.
facts.quote: It is known from a single tooth usually referred to the contemporaneous "wastebasket taxon" Pelorosaurus, although there is no solid evidence for this.

facts.statement: A large reptilian tooth was reported by geologist Thomas Wright in 1852 from the Wealden Clay near Brixton Bay on the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: In 1852 geologist Thomas Wright reported the find of a large reptilian tooth from the Wealden Clay near Brixton Bay on Wight.

facts.statement: French paleontologist Paul Gervais established the type species Oplosaurus armatus in 1852 based on the tooth found by Thomas Wright.
facts.quote: Gervais in 1852 based the type species Oplosaurus armatus on it.

facts.statement: The holotype tooth of Oplosaurus is 85 mm tall in total, with a spatulate crown measuring 52 mm, a size comparable to that of Brachiosaurus.
facts.quote: The tooth is large, 85 mm (3.35 in) tall in total, with a spatulate crown 52 mm (2.05 in) tall, comparable to Brachiosaurus

facts.statement: The generic name Oplosaurus is derived from the Greek word hoplon, which means "body armour".
facts.quote: The generic name would normally read as "armoured lizard" from the Greek hoplon, "body armour".

facts.statement: Recent research suggests Paul Gervais may have intended the name Oplosaurus to mean "armed lizard," interpreting the teeth as weapons of a carnivore rather than armor.
facts.quote: However, recent research by Ben Creisler shows that Gervais compared it to Mosasaurus, not Hylaeosaurus, and that the name may have been intended as "armed lizard", with the teeth as the weapons of a carnivore

facts.statement: Richard Lydekker suggested in 1888 that a maxilla with a tooth from the Isle of Wight belonged to Oplosaurus, but this opinion has not been substantiated.
facts.quote: Richard Lydekker (1888) suggested that a maxilla with a tooth (BMNH R751), also from the Isle of Wight, was another exemplar of this animal, but this opinion has not been substantiated.

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene suggested in 1909 that Oplosaurus should be referred to the genus Pelorosaurus.
facts.quote: Earlier, Oplosaurus was typically referred to Pelorosaurus following an opinion of Friedrich von Huene in 1909

facts.statement: Darren Naish has informally suggested that Oplosaurus may be a turiasaur, while also co-authoring an article concluding it was a member of the Camarasauridae.
facts.quote: Darren Naish, a British palaeontologist familiar with Wealden sauropods, has suggested informally that the genus may be a turiasaur but also co-authored an article concluding it was a member of the Camarasauridae.

facts.statement: Oplosaurus armatus is the only known species of the dubious extinct genus Oplosaurus, a sauropod dinosaur that lived approximately 130 million years ago during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: Oplosaurus armatus es la única especie conocida del género dudoso extinto Oplosaurus (gr. "arma de lagarto") de dinosaurio saurópodo turiasauriano, que vivió en el Cretácico inferior, hace aproximadamente 130 millones de años, en el Barremiense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Oplosaurus lived between the Valanginian and Barremian stages, approximately 137.05 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Barremian (137.05 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The size of the Oplosaurus tooth, comparable to that of Brachiosaurus, indicates the animal was a large sauropod, a conclusion that holds even if it is classified as a turiasaur.
facts.quote: As Naish and Martill point out, the tooth is comparable in size to that of Brachiosaurus, indicating that the owner was a large sauropod; as a possible turiasaur, the size should not change drastically.

facts.statement: Oplosaurus was likely a quadrupedal herbivore reaching a length of approximately 25 meters (82 feet).
facts.quote: It would have been a quadrupedal herbivore, possibly around 25 m (82 ft) long.

facts.statement: Oplosaurus likely belongs to the broader group Macronaria.
facts.quote: In any case, it likely belongs to the more general Macronaria.

facts.statement: Regardless of specific family placement, Oplosaurus likely belongs to the general group Macronaria.
facts.quote: En cualquier caso, probablemente pertenece a la Macronaria más general.

facts.statement: There is an open debate regarding the classification of Oplosaurus, with some researchers suggesting it is a turiasaur while others conclude it is a member of the Camarasauridae.
facts.quote: Darren Naish, a British palaeontologist familiar with Wealden sauropods, has suggested informally that the genus may be a turiasaur but also co-authored an article concluding it was a member of the Camarasauridae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the name Oplosaurus originally referred to an armored dinosaur or an armed carnivore, with recent research suggesting Gervais compared the tooth to Mosasaurus rather than Hylaeosaurus.
facts.quote: However, recent research by Ben Creisler shows that Gervais compared it to Mosasaurus, not Hylaeosaurus, and that the name may have been intended as "armed lizard", with the teeth as the weapons of a carnivore
